anomaly_def.Name: Schema and Index Design Anomaly + Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly + Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Schema and Index Design Anomaly : The physical data model (tables, indexes, partitions, data types, constraints) is mis-aligned with workload access patterns, forcing otherwise well-written queries into systematically inefficient access paths.
Data Block and Index Integrity Anomaly : On-disk table and index pages are internally corrupted or mutually inconsistent, so logical rows can be missing, duplicated, or inaccessible even when the optimizer selects the right access path.
Network and Connectivity Resource Anomaly : The transport layer between clients and the DBMS cannot sustain offered load because of link congestion, packet loss, handshake/ authentication limits, or exhausted connection slots, causing frequent connect and I/O stalls.

When these three root causes coexist, the system exhibits compound symptoms across all tiers: 1) query plans already slowed by poor or absent indexing fall back to full scans, which in turn traverse corrupted pages and trigger corruption errors, retries, or silent data mismatches; 2) corruption-induced retries, error logging, or engine failovers amplify session churn, driving up connection establishment rates until listener backlogs overflow, producing client timeouts and half-open sockets; 3) network stalls elongate transaction times, so more concurrent sessions hold locks while simultaneously performing scan-heavy I/O against damaged structures, inflating buffer-pool churn, latch contention, and recovery events; 4) monitoring shows a mix of slow logical query metrics, sporadic "row not found" or "checksum failure" messages, and rising connection-related wait events, making root-cause isolation difficult because each layer’s symptoms obscure the others.

Causally, the misdesigned schema initiates excessive full-table/ index activity that increases physical page touch-rate, heightening the probability of encountering latent block or index corruption; once such corruption manifests, queries repeatedly fail or fall back to even more expensive scans, magnifying load. The resultant latency and retry storms overload client connection pools and database listener resources, feeding a feedback loop where network congestion and authentication bottlenecks prolong transactions, further stressing the flawed schema and exposing additional corrupt pages. Together, the structural inefficiency, physical corruption, and connectivity saturation reinforce each other, rapidly degrading both throughput and data correctness across transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
